notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Read existing sibling functions to infer conventions before implementing: The first attempt passed visible tests but was rejected for missing a rounding convention that sibling functions already followed.
  When adding a function to a module, inspect neighboring functions for patterns (rounding, type hints, zero-handling) and apply them consistently. Passing the visible test suite is not sufficient evidence that team conventions are met.
- [rb-0006] Normalize money before range checks: Round/normalize monetary inputs via the project's money helper before comparing against zero so validation matches stored values.
  Call round_money(unit_price) first, then compare the rounded Decimal against ZERO. This ensures the stored value and the validation agree, and lets the helper raise its own errors (e.g. float_amount) for bad types.
- [rb-0001] Round monetary results with the project's round_money helper: Money values must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in the repository's round_money helper. Check the money module for existing conventions (ZERO, to_money, round_money) and mirror how sibling functions like line_total and invoice_total round their results.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly with the project's ZERO constant: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
  Compute the denominator first, return ZERO (imported from the money module) if it is falsy, and only then perform the division. Use sum(..., ZERO) with an explicit start value so empty sequences yield a Decimal rather than int 0.
- [rb-0004] Mirror existing validation patterns in the module: Reuse the error codes, state checks, and money helpers already used by sibling functions to stay consistent with hidden tests.
  Before implementing a new function, read sibling functions (e.g. issue_invoice, authorize) to copy their exact BillingError codes and message formats. Reuse existing helpers like round_money, to_money, and ZERO rather than reimplementing money handling.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool when validating integer inputs: In Python, bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly reject bools for integer-only parameters.
  When a parameter must be a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. This catches True/False and floats that would otherwise slip through or silently truncate.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any validation
item.description: When a team convention requires idempotency, look up the audit log for the key first, before validating state or amounts, and return the original result.
item.content: Scan audit.events(<event>) for a matching idempotency_key at the very top of the function and return the stored record unchanged. Only after that miss do amount/state checks; include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Honor approval-threshold conventions on money moves
item.description: Support refunds/credits above a fixed threshold need a second approver; add keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError('approval_required') when missing.
item.content: Define a module-level APPROVAL_THRESHOLD (e.g. round_money('500.00')) and gate amounts strictly above it. Keep the parameter keyword-only with a default so existing callers without approval still work for small amounts.

item.title: Mirror sibling module patterns for new functions
item.description: Before implementing a stub, read sibling functions (payments.py) and shared helpers (money, clock, errors, audit) to copy rounding, validation order, and error codes.
item.content: Reuse round_money/ZERO for all arithmetic, ensure_utc(at) for timestamps, and BillingError with the same code style (non_positive_amount, invalid_state) as existing functions. This keeps hidden tests and conventions satisfied without guessing.
